items.title: Your rent, your neighbourhood, your commute: Which Mississauga mayoral candidates actually have a plan?
items.summary: Here’s how some mayoral candidates plan to fix transit, build affordable homes, and enforce property standards. Candidates were asked how they would improve MiWay’s access, speed, and reliability to reverse declining ridership, and if they support expanding the transit network. Housing affordability, declining ridership on MiWay, and increasing citywide littering and illegal dumping are some other important issues residents are discussing in Mississauga ahead of the Oct. 26 election. We offered mayoral candidates an opportunity to share how they plan to address these challenges. Candidates were invited to response to two questions: Some responses have been edited for clarity. Mississauga needs more housing that ordinary working families can actually afford. I would work to accelerate approvals, encourage purpose-built rental and affordable housing, make better use of city-owned land, and work with other levels of government to increase the supply of genuinely affordable homes — not simply more expensive market housing. Residents should not have to repeatedly complain before basic property standards are enforced. I would support consistent, city-wide enforcement, faster response times, transparent tracking of complaints and adequate resources in areas experiencing higher volumes of violations. MiWay must be more reliable, accessible, and responsive to residents. I support expanding the network where there is demonstrated demand, improving frequency, and connecting underserved communities. Transit planning must reflect where people actually live, work and travel.

items.title: 4 Mississauga mayoral candidates invited to Port Credit debate Thursday
items.summary: At the debate, organized by the Town of Port Credit and Lakeview Ratepayers associations, candidates will address key municipal issues, including taxes, transit, and intensification. The four mayoral candidates invited to a mayoral debate in Port Credit. Clockwise from top left: Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Alvin Tedjo and Carolyn Parrish. With the municipal election set for Oct. 26, residents in Mississauga will have the opportunity to hear four invited mayoral candidates during a resident-led debate Thursday, Oct. 15. Organized by the Town of Port Credit Association and Lakeview Ratepayers’ Association, the debate is being hosted at Christ First United Church in Port Credit and is open for residents across the city to attend. The venue, located at 151 Lakeshore Rd. , according to a press release. Mayoral candidates Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo will be participating, with the debate focused on key municipal issues, including property taxes, citywide intensification, transit and infrastructure. Candidates will also respond to questions about provincial decision-making, strong-mayor powers and Mississauga’s provincial funding allocations. Residents will have the floor to ask questions from the candidates after the debate portion of the event.

items.title: Largest art show and sale in Mississauga celebrates 25 years
items.summary: The largest art show and sale in Mississauga celebrates 25 years this weekend. The Lakeshore Art Trail’s Art Show & Sale, featuring over 40 artists, is on this Saturday and Sunday at the Small Arms Inspection Building. For over 25 years, the Lakeshore Art Trail has strengthened the local arts scene, supported artists at all stages of their careers, and created meaningful opportunities for the community to experience and celebrate the visual arts, organizers said. “LAT has become the largest fine art show and sale in Mississauga with 40 exhibiting artists, and has its sights set on growing over the next few years to bring a show of the same size and calibre as Toronto and other GTA arts events to Mississauga,” the organizers said in a press release. The Lakeshore Art Trail is organized by an artist-run executive committee. Previously, participating artists showcased their creations out of their studios or local businesses across Clarkson, Port Credit and Lorne Park. In 2022, the event changed its location to the Small Arms Inspection Building in partnership with CreativeHub 1352 for the first time, bringing together all 24 artists to display and sell their work under one roof. Over 2,000 visitors attended that first year. Each year, the show continues to grow, and the committee expects to welcome over 4,000 visitors throughout the weekend event this year.

items.title: Attempted murder charges follow road rage stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: Police have charged a man with two counts of attempted murder as they investigate a Mississauga road rage incident in which two men were attacked and stabbed in a parking lot. m. on Aug. 29, a Saturday, in a parking lot near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road, a couple of blocks east of Mavis Road. “Investigators determined that a road rage incident in a parking lot escalated into a confrontation between the occupants of two vehicles, resulting in two individuals being stabbed,” police said, adding both victims were transported to hospital with serious injuries. They were later reported to be in stable condition. Shortly after the incident, uniformed officers located and arrested one suspect, police added. He was charged with one count of assault. Continuing their probe, detectives with the Peel police 11 Division Criminal Investigations Bureau subsequently arrested and charged a second man in connection with the stabbing investigation. Isaiah Myles, 26, of Mississauga, was arrested on Oct. 1, according to police. He was charged with two counts of attempted murder and held in custody pending a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Ali Halimi, 30, also of Mississauga, who was arrested in August, is charged with assault. Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said the latest arrest is “another important step” in the ongoing investigation.

items.title: Mississauga Seeks Volunteers to Bring Back Dozens of Neighbourhood Ice Rinks This Winter
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga is calling on volunteers to bring back its Natural Ice Rinks Program for another winter season. According to the outlet, dozens of neighbourhood parks across the city rely on volunteer rink-keepers to build and maintain outdoor ice surfaces once temperatures turn cold enough, typically by late December or January. The city says anyone willing to help must be at least 14 years old and comfortable working outside in winter conditions, often in the evening after dark. Applications are due by Nov. 15, the outlet reports. Unlike larger indoor facilities, insauga.com notes these community rinks exist only because local volunteers show up to care for them through the season, giving residents free spots to skate or play pickup hockey at locations ranging from Celebration Square downtown to parks throughout the city's neighbourhoods. City officials describe the program as a longstanding winter tradition in Mississauga and across Canada.

items.title: Road Rage Clash on Dundas Street West Leads to Second Arrest in Mississauga Stabbing
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a second suspect has been arrested and charged with attempted murder in connection with a Mississauga stabbing that began as a road rage dispute. According to investigators, officers responded in August to a confrontation near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road after an argument between the occupants of two vehicles turned violent in a parking lot, leaving two people stabbed and taken to hospital with serious injuries. Police say a first suspect, 30-year-old Ali Halimi of Mississauga, was arrested at the scene shortly afterward and charged with assault. Investigators with the 11 Division Criminal Investigations Bureau say the second suspect, 26-year-old Isaiah Myles of Mississauga, was arrested on Oct. 1 and held for a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Peel Regional Police describe the arrest as an important step in an investigation they say remains ongoing, and ask anyone with information to contact the 11 Division unit.

items.title: Mississauga’s fall colours return to parks and trails across the city
items.summary: Discover vibrant views, scenic trails and some of the best places for sightseeing this season. As temperatures cool and leaves begin to change, Mississauga’s annual display of fall colours is under way. Filled with vibrant reds, oranges, yellows and golds, the city’s trails, parks and other natural areas offer plenty of opportunities to take in the sights of the season close to home. Mid-October through early November is typically one of the best times to experience autumn colours in Mississauga. Whether you’re looking for a peaceful walk, a family outing, a cycling route or the perfect seasonal photo, there are countless places across the city to take in the changing landscape. One of the best things about fall in Mississauga is seeing the city’s urban forest come to life with colour. More than two million trees help create a brilliant seasonal backdrop that can be enjoyed from neighbourhood parks, waterfront trails and natural areas across the city. Looking for the best spots to see fall colours this season? From iconic natural areas to hidden neighbourhood gems, these destinations offer unique ways to experience Mississauga’s changing landscape. Located in the heart of the city, Riverwood offers one of Mississauga’s most picturesque fall experiences. Visitors can explore trails winding through mature forests, meadows, ravines and wetlands while enjoying colourful tree canopies and opportunities to spot local wildlife. Set alongside the Credit River, Streetsville Memorial Park provides beautiful riverside views framed by autumn foliage. After exploring the park, visitors can stroll through the nearby village of Streetsville and enjoy local shops, cafés and restaurants. For those looking to spend more time outdoors, Meadowvale Conservation Area features scenic trails, open spaces and natural heritage features surrounded by changing leaves.

items.title: Family Medicine Forum, Canada’s largest family medicine celebration, returns to Toronto this November
items.summary: This content may have been approved or produced by a partner MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Family Medicine Forum (FMF) is back in Toronto, November 11th to 14th, for four days of learning, networking, and celebrating family medicine. MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Family Medicine Forum (FMF) is back in Toronto, November 11th to 14th, for four days of learning, networking, and celebrating family medicine. The largest annual family medicine conference in Canada is hosted by the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CFPC). FMF 2026 is where Canada’s family physicians come together to learn, share knowledge, and strengthen the future of family medicine. “FMF is one of the highlights of my year,” said Dr. Sarah Cook, CFPC President. “The energy is incredible – from the buzz of conversation to those unforgettable moments that bring everyone in a room to their feet. FMF showcases the best of family medicine and the strength of our community. It’s a chance to learn and connect and be inspired by what we can achieve together. ” “Every year, I leave FMF with new ideas, fresh perspectives, and a renewed appreciation for our profession,” said CFPC CEO Dr. Mike Allan. “Convocation is a particular highlight, as we welcome new family doctors into the CFPC family and celebrate the future of family medicine.
